title: Scramble
description: Text that decodes itself: glyphs churn, then settle into the word, left to right.
usage: For short, loud strings — a title, a status line, a launch date. The script runs when the element scrolls into view and again whenever it is clicked. Long sentences scramble into noise; keep it under a dozen characters per burst if you can.
a11y: The real string is the element’s text and its aria-label from the start; the churn is aria-hidden theatre in a sibling span. Under prefers-reduced-motion there is no churn at all — the word simply stands there, decoded since birth.
